tepjf_constituyentes_1916.note: Read 2026-11-14. The convocatoria (Carranza, 19 September 1916) set direct election on Sunday 22 October 1916 on the 1910 census and the 1912 division into electoral districts; the same article puts that division at 244 districts and says the election was held in 216 of them, not in Campeche, Quintana Roo, or the parts of Chihuahua and Morelos held by Villa and Zapata. The INEHRM biographical dictionary of the constituent deputies says 215.

Contests are counted as 300 districts plus 5 circunscripciones.

classes.name: Elección de personas juzgadoras del Poder Judicial de la Federación
classes.note: Since the judicial reform of 15 September 2024, Supreme Court justices, Judicial Discipline Tribunal and Electoral Tribunal magistrates, circuit magistrates, and district judges are elected by popular vote from lists nominated by the three branches, nationally, by circuit, or by judicial electoral district (CPEUM arts. 94-97). First held 1 June 2025 for 881 posts with about 13% turnout; the decree of 2 June 2026 moved the next election, for every post not renewed in 2025, to the first Sunday of June 2028, coinciding with the state judicial elections.

classes.name: Designación de Presidente interino o sustituto por el Congreso
classes.name_en: Interim and substitute presidents chosen by Congress
classes.note: When the presidency falls vacant, Congress (or its Permanent Commission) names an interim or substitute president by secret ballot of an absolute majority (CPEUM arts. 84-85): Adolfo de la Huerta 1920, Emilio Portes Gil 1928, and Abelardo L. Rodríguez 1932. The record is the Diario de los Debates.

classes.name: Congreso Constituyente de 1916-1917
classes.note: Elected by direct vote in single-member districts on 22 October 1916, on the 1912 division of 244 districts (the election was held in 216 of them); it wrote the Constitution of 1917. The record is the Diario de los Debates del Congreso Constituyente.

classes.name: Elecciones presidenciales indirectas (1824-1911)
classes.note: Under the constitutions of 1824 and 1857 the president was chosen indirectly: by the state legislatures (1824-1853) and then by electoral colleges of electors chosen in primary elections (1857-1911, Madero's election of 1911 the last). Votes are electors' and legislatures' votes from the Diario de los Debates and Congress's declarations; no popular counts survive for most years.

classes.name: Elecciones al Congreso de la Unión (1822-1916)
classes.note: Congresses of the Empire, the First Federal Republic, the centralist republics, and the Restored Republic and Porfiriato, elected indirectly through electors until the Ley Electoral of 1911 made deputy elections direct (first held 30 June 1912). Senate restored in 1874.

classes.name: Elección de Gubernaturas y de la Jefatura de Gobierno
classes.name_en: State governors and the Head of Government of Mexico City
classes.note: Each state elects its governor by plurality for six years with no re-election (CPEUM art. 116 I); Mexico City elects its Head of Government since 1997 (art. 122). Each state's constitution sets the year; terms were shortened or lengthened between 2015 and 2022 so that every state votes with a federal election (Aguascalientes and Quintana Roo, elected in 2022, vote again in 2027). Extraordinary elections (Colima 2016, Puebla 2019) belong here.

classes.name: Elección de los Congresos de los Estados y de la Ciudad de México
classes.name_en: State legislatures and the Congress of Mexico City
classes.note: Unicameral, elected for three years by plurality in local districts and by proportional representation (CPEUM art. 116 II); consecutive re-election up to four terms since 2018. Mexico City's Asamblea de Representantes (1988-1994), Asamblea Legislativa (1997-2015), and Congress (since 2018) belong here; the 2016 constituent assembly is its own class. Some states add a migrant deputy.

classes.name: Asamblea Constituyente de la Ciudad de México
classes.note: 60 of its 100 members elected on 5 June 2016 from lists in a single Mexico City constituency by proportional representation; the other 40 were appointed. It wrote the Constitution of Mexico City.

classes.name: Elección de Ayuntamientos
classes.note: Each municipality elects its ayuntamiento, a municipal president, one or more síndicos, and regidores, as a closed slate (planilla) by plurality, with proportional regidores, for three years; consecutive re-election once since 2018 (CPEUM art. 115 I). Contests count municipal presidencies. Municipalities that elect by indigenous normative systems are the class ayuntamiento_sni.

classes.name: Elección de Ayuntamientos por sistemas normativos indígenas
classes.name_en: Municipal authorities elected by indigenous normative systems (usos y costumbres)
classes.note: 418 Oaxaca municipalities (IEEPCO catalog 2025) elect their authorities in community assemblies by show of hands, ballots, or other customary methods, on dates and terms (one to three years) each community sets; IEEPCO validates each election. Elsewhere Cherán (Michoacán, since 2011), Ayutla de los Libres (Guerrero, since 2018), and Oxchuc (Chiapas, since 2019) elect the same way. Results are rulings naming those elected, rarely vote counts.

classes.name: Elección de las Comisiones de Participación Comunitaria (COPACO)

Elected in 2020, 2023, and 2026 (online 20-30 April, in person 3 May 2026).

classes.name: Procesos internos de los partidos
classes.name_en: Party primaries, conventions, and leadership votes
classes.note: Parties choose candidates by conventions, polls, or member votes under their statutes; INE organizes a party's leadership vote only at its request (LGIPE art. 32.2 b).
classes.disposition_reason: Party-internal processes the state does not run or certify as elections; INE's occasional organization of a leadership vote at a party's request (PRD 2014) publishes no comparable results.

classes.name: Votaciones sindicales y gremiales
classes.disposition_reason: Workplace and professional votes (union leadership and collective contract votes verified by the Centro Federal de Conciliación y Registro Laboral since 2019); not public elections.

classes.name: Consultas organizadas por gobiernos sin autoridad electoral
classes.name_en: Government consultations run without an electoral authority
classes.disposition_reason: Polls run by a government or its transition team rather than INE or an OPLE (the 2018 airport and 2018-2019 infrastructure consultations), and indigenous consultations under ILO Convention 169 held by assemblies; no electoral authority counted the votes.
